summary: Older L-4 cab from the 1950s Franson Peak tower, moved to the Molson Museum in Okanogan County when the current Franson structure was built in 1986.

facts.design: L-4 cab from the 1950s 15-ft treated timber tower at Franson Peak

access.note: Molson Museums say there is no fee to visit either museum and accept donations. Okanogan Country describes the cab as a ground-level display. The museums do not plow for access during snow events.

visit.trail_note: From Oroville, east on Chesaw Road to Molson Road, then about 5 miles to the town of Molson. Sources differ on the first leg (about 9 miles per Okanogan Country, 10 miles per Molson Museums).

events.note: The older L-4 cab moved from Franson Peak to the Molson Museum when the current 15-ft structure was built.

evidence.supports: Franson Peak developed in 1934 with an L-5 cab; 1950s 15-ft timber tower with L-4 cab replaced it
evidence.quote: Franson Peak was developed in 1934 with an L-5 cab, then a 15′ treated timber tower with L-4 cab replaced it in the 1950s

evidence.supports: L-4 cab moved to the Molson Museum when the current structure went up
evidence.quote: That L-4 cab was moved to the Molson Museum when the current structure

evidence.supports: current 15-ft tower with DNR live-in cab built in 1986
evidence.quote: A 15′ tower with DNR live-in cab, was built in 1986

evidence.supports: Franson last staffed in 1995; Aircraft Warning Service 1942
Aircraft Warning Service site March to October 1942
evidence.quote: Franson Peak served as an Aircraft Warning Service site from March to October 1942

evidence.supports: 1986 move of the 1950s cab to the Molson Museum
evidence.quote: When the current structure was built in 1986, the 1950s cab was relocated to the Molson Museum

evidence.supports: Franson Peak lies in Ferry County, next to the Okanogan County side where the cab is
evidence.quote: The Franson Peak Lookout location is in our neighboring county of Ferry

evidence.supports: Molson is a ghost town east of Oroville
evidence.quote: lands you in a remote ghost town east of Oroville

evidence.supports: cab is shown at ground level
evidence.quote: Check out the historic cab at ground level

evidence.supports: cab sits with the Schoolhouse Museum
evidence.quote: with the Franson Cab and the Schoolhouse Museum on the left

evidence.quote: The drive is possible with a 4x4 vehicle, but there is an easier way to see one of the older cabs

evidence.supports: Okanogan Country directions: about 9 miles on Chesaw Road to Molson Road
evidence.quote: drive east on Chesaw road approximately 9 miles to Molson Rd

evidence.supports: Molson Museums directions: 10 miles on Chesaw Road
evidence.quote: Follow Chesaw Road for 10 miles until you see Molson Road on the left

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Okanogan Country gives about 9 miles on Chesaw Road to Molson Road; the Molson Museums give 10 miles. Both are reported in the story; check before driving.

notes_for_editor: The brief says 'None relocated' with no year. The 1986 date comes from NHLR and Okanogan Country, which agree. The 1950s date for the L-4 cab is only a decade in both sources, so no year is given for the cab's tower. The story covers the cab only; the summit history is in data/stories/us-wa-franson-peak.md, where the 1934-vs-1986 build-year conflict is still open. The Molson Museums' hours and fees come from their own page and should be rechecked before a visit. The cab's exact display spot was not confirmed on a museum page.
